intro.title: Real-time systems
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple real-time system simulation to understand how systems process tasks with strict timing requirements. You will learn the core concept of real-time constraints, distinguishing between hard and soft real-time systems. The main technologies involved are event-driven programming and timing mechanisms to model task scheduling. By the end, you will be able to implement a basic real-time task scheduler and evaluate its performance against deadlines.
intro.usecase: Real-time systems are critical in modern applications where immediate data processing and response are essential. In financial trading platforms, real-time systems process market data feeds to execute trades within milliseconds, preventing financial losses. Live sports tracking apps use real-time systems to update scores, player statistics, and play-by-play commentary instantly for millions of concurrent viewers. Industrial control systems in manufacturing rely on real-time processing to monitor sensors and adjust machinery parameters to maintain production quality and safety. These systems require predictable latency and high reliability, making their design principles fundamental for developers building time-sensitive applications.
